title: Ibuprofen & COX: cuts new prostaglandins
topic: How ibuprofen reversibly plugs COX to cut new PGE₂, and why it can't erase prostaglandins already sensitising pulpal nerves.

claims.claim: Inflamed pulp frees arachidonic acid (PLA₂ cuts it from membrane phospholipids)
claims.source: Funk CD, Science 2001;294:1871-5 (PMID 11729303); pulp anchor (PGE₂ ↑ in inflamed pulp): Nakanishi T et al., J Endod 1995;21:131-6 (PMID 7561655)

claims.claim: COX-1/COX-2 make PGH₂ (AA → PGG₂ → PGH₂); PGE synthase converts it to PGE₂, which leaves the cell
claims.source: Smith WL et al., Annu Rev Biochem 2000;69:145-82 (PMID 10966456); Park JY et al., Clin Immunol 2006;119:229-40 (PMID 16540375)
Nakanishi T et al., J Endod 2001;27:385-8 (PMID 11487130)

claims.claim: PGE₂ on nociceptor EP receptors lowers the firing threshold
Ibuprofen reversibly (competitively) plugs the COX channel; one AA can slip through when it unbinds
claims.source: Selinsky BS et al., Biochemistry 2001;40:5172-80 (PMID 11318639); Orlando BJ et al., J Struct Biol 2015;189:62-6 (PMID 25463020)

claims.claim: Less new PGE₂ → nerve calms, but only partly (threshold recovers partway)
claims.source: Kawabata A, Biol Pharm Bull 2011;34:1170-3 (PMID 21804201); Nguyen V et al., J Endod 2020;46:1210-6 (PMID 32565333); Bowles WR et al., J Endod 2003;29:265-7 (PMID 12701777)

claims.claim: Other mediators (e.g. substance P) still act
claims.source: Bowles WR et al., J Endod 2003;29:265-7 (PMID 12701777)

claims.claim: Ibuprofen cuts NEW prostaglandins; it can't erase the ones already made
claims.source: Vane JR, Nat New Biol 1971;231:232-5 (PMID 5284360); Smith WL et al., Annu Rev Biochem 2000;69:145-82 (PMID 10966456); Selinsky BS et al., Biochemistry 2001;40:5172-80 (PMID 11318639); Nguyen V et al., J Endod 2020;46:1210-6 (PMID 32565333)

claims.claim: One rationale for dosing before treatment: pre-op NSAIDs aid IANB success; post-op pain benefit unclear
claims.source: Shirvani A et al., Clin Oral Investig 2017;21:43-52 (PMID 27837343); Nagendrababu V et al., J Endod 2018;44:914-922.e2 (PMID 29709297); de Geus JL et al., Eur Endod J 2018;3:123-33 (PMID 32161868)

caption:
What ibuprofen can't undo.

In inflamed pulp, COX (COX-2 up) turns arachidonic acid into PGE₂, which lowers the nerve's firing threshold.
Ibuprofen reversibly plugs the COX channel: less NEW PGE₂, not zero.
It can't erase what's already made, and other mediators (e.g. substance P) still act.
One rationale for dosing before treatment: pre-op NSAIDs aid IANB success in irreversible pulpitis; post-op pain benefit is unclear.

Refs: Vane 1971, Nat New Biol; Selinsky 2001, Biochemistry; Nakanishi 2001, J Endod; Kawabata 2011, Biol Pharm Bull; Bowles 2003, J Endod; Shirvani 2017, Clin Oral Investig; Nagendrababu 2018, J Endod; de Geus 2018, Eur Endod J; Nguyen 2020, J Endod
Animation is schematic (toy counts, time compressed).
